svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.15.2 Area and Location of Exposing Building Face
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Area and Location of Exposing Building Face

g.text: Area of the exposing building face
one direction, from finished ground level to the
uppermost ceiling, the gable above is not counted
Area of the face as a whole
Three portions, each with its own limiting distance
for the glazing of Table 9.10.15.4., Subclause (1)(b)(iii)
Portions are not limited to equal sizes (Note)
One room, limiting distance 2 m (6′-6¾″) or less
its section of the face is not divided into

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
The area of an exposing building face is the exterior wall area
facing in one direction on any side of a building
Calculated as (i) the total area from the finished ground level to the
uppermost ceiling, (ii) reserved, or (iii) except as in Sentence (2),
where Table 9.10.15.4. is used for the maximum aggregate area of
glazed openings, the area of any number of individual portions of the
face. Except as permitted by Sentence (5). See Note A-9.10.15.4.(2).
A section of the face enclosing a single room or space, or
combination room and space, with a limiting distance of 2 m
(6′-6¾″) or less, is not divided into portions
For calculating the area of exposing building face. See Sentence
For Table 9.10.15.4. and an irregularly shaped or skewed wall,
the face is a vertical plane with no glazed openings between it
and the line to which the limiting distance is measured
For the cladding-sheathing assembly and fire-resistance rating
of such a wall, the face is a vertical plane with no portion of
the actual face between it and that line
See Article 9.10.15.5. and Note A-3.2.3.1.(4).
Where a building is divided by fire separations into fire
compartments, the area may be calculated for each fire
compartment
Provided the fire separations have a fire-resistance rating not less
than 45 min.
Where a face is stepped back from or at an angle to the property line,
glazing can be increased in the portions further away without
increasing the radiated energy reaching the property line. The face
can be divided into any number of portions, not necessarily of equal
size. Each limiting distance is measured perpendicular to the wall
from the point closest to the property line.
Drawn: in A and B red is the face area. C and D are plans cut low, the beige floor in C is one room.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.15.2. (page 9-87)
